transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Alvarez (Redwood AE), Markus Li (Redwood SE), Lauren Chen (BluePeak Head of Platform), Tomas Rivera (BluePeak SRE), Priya Nair (BluePeak CISO)

Summary:
Quick post-escalation sync to walk through the 11/07 surge-decay incident, validate mitigations, agree pilot scope and an escrow-style fallback plan for sensitive customers. Action items and security signoffs required before pilot.

Topics covered:
- Incident timeline and surge-decay pattern (KV cache warm/cool behavior)
- Tail latency regression and inter-region routing behavior
- Data security: VPC peering, KMS/HSM, SAML/SSO, audit logs retention
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, cost modeling and SLA expectations
- Pilot/escrow plan and next steps (benchmarks, permissions, canary)

Action items (in-call - also in metadata):
- Sofia to share trimmed benchmark results and the raw logs (token-level) by Fri 11/13
- Markus to provision Dedicated trial and run a 3-hour tail-latency workload by Wed 11/18
- BluePeak to deliver prompt corpus and PII redaction rules by Sun 11/15
- Priya to confirm KMS/SSO approvals and send policy extract by Mon 11/16

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Alvarez: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick readout, we wanted to make sure we walked the timeline with you and also land the next steps for that escrow fallback plan for the biggest accounts. Are we all good on time?
[00:10] Lauren Chen: Yep, we can go. Appreciate it. Sorry, last week was messy with the racks flipping over, so —
[00:15] Tomas Rivera: yeah, the surge-decay really caught our edge cases. We saw long tail spike then like 20 minutes of decayed throughput, then another micro-surge.
[00:27] Markus Li: Right, the pattern we saw on Redwood side matched the KV-cache eviction timing plus a regional routing thrash. There's a couple of places where the default batching policy stepped in and increased latency.
[00:40] Priya Nair: I wanted to flag security first: we need clarity on where logs live and how long they're retained. SOC2 doc pointers? KMS, HSM, that's a must.
[00:50] Sofia Alvarez: Absolutely. We'll share the SOC2 checklist, the KMS integration doc and the audit log retention table. Quick caveat, some of the field names in the logs are abbreviated; there may be transcription-ish names like 'kv' or 'k v' depending on the exporter.
[01:05] Tomas Rivera: we also saw some mis-attributed metrics in our dashboards, sometimes the instance tags flipped. Could that be a sampling artifact?
[01:13] Markus Li: Possibly. The sampling window + autoscaler jitter can create intermittent misattribution. We'll include the raw trace spans so you can correlate.
[02:20] Lauren Chen: Can you restate the proposed escrow plan? I want to make sure my folks understand the rollback pages.
[02:27] Sofia Alvarez: Sure. The idea is an escrow-style fallback where, during the pilot, if latencies exceed the agreed SLO we automatically route to a hardened model variant in Dedicated capacity and enable more aggressive caching. It's like a temporary seats handoff - automatic fallover plus a customer-held escrow for logs and config.
[02:46] Tomas Rivera: so we'd have Dedicated reserved capacity spun up on demand? That's costy.
[02:50] Markus Li: We recommended a small burst pool - think of it as warm-standby. It's cheaper than full-reservation but gives predictable tail behavior. We'll provide a cost delta spreadsheet.
[03:10] Priya Nair: For legal and compliance we need to document what 'on demand' means: audit trail, who can trigger, TTL of the dedicated pool, and whether it's permissive to auto-scale.
[03:25] Sofia Alvarez: Yep. We'll add an approval workflow: BluePeak on-call approves the trigger, Redwood can also auto-trigger with a 2-minute mute window and immediate notification. All triggers logged to your audit bucket.
[04:00] Tomas Rivera: a question on the root cause: you mentioned kernel selection and quantization paths earlier in the postmortem?
[04:08] Markus Li: Yeah, two factors. One was kernel choice for the long-context sequences; the other was a quantization mismatch between the cached kv entries and the newer model variant which caused cache misses. The cache TTL and serialization format were slightly incompatible after the rollout.
[04:33] Lauren Chen: so cache corruption? or format drift?
[04:36] Markus Li: More format drift + eviction timing. Not corruption per se. We have a fix to normalize serialization across variants and a migration job to rehydrate cache entries.
[05:00] Sofia Alvarez: We'll share the migration script and a safe rollout plan. It's non-destructive but we will stage it in Canary first.
[05:15] Tomas Rivera: Canary on, say, 5% traffic?
[05:19] Markus Li: Yeah 5% with an automatic rollback on tail latency threshold. Also we'll lock the model pin for the canary and keep a cross-region mirror to compare.
[06:00] Priya Nair: On the KMS front, do you support customer-managed keys and HSM integration? We can't have Redwood hold the only key.
[06:09] Sofia Alvarez: Yes we support CMKs via standard KMS integrations and HSM for Private deployments. We'll share the integration pattern. For Hosted we support a bring-your-own-KMS option for encryption at rest of customer artifacts.
[06:30] Tomas Rivera: And what about VPC? We need peering and private links; can't have data egress to public endpoints for this workload.
[06:38] Markus Li: Private deployments include VPC peering or private link depending on cloud provider. For the trial, we can do dedicated VPC peering with strict egress controls and flow logs forwarded to your SIEM.
[07:00] Lauren Chen: cost modeling — can you show unit economics for the warm standby? We need a monthly delta number and a per-10k-requests incremental cost so finance can sign off.
[07:10] Sofia Alvarez: We'll send a spreadsheet. Quick ballpark: warm standby (small Dedicated pool) added about 12-18% to our normal per-token cost for the scenarios in the benchmark. We'll attach the assumptions.
[07:40] Tomas Rivera: One of our engineers mentioned earlier there might be mis-parsed product names in the logs - like 'Redwood Dedicated' appearing as 'red wood ded' or something. Is that from the exporter?
[07:49] Markus Li: Heh, yeah exporters sometimes slug the names; we'll unify the naming and include a mapping table.
[08:20] Lauren Chen: Are we running an A/B or a direct routing test for the pilot?
[08:25] Markus Li: We'll recommend canary (A/B) at the routing layer with trace-level comparison. That lets you see differences without impacting all traffic.
[08:40] Priya Nair: For the security packet, we'll need: SOC2 attestation, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS key control proof, SIEM integration guide, and a short SLA matrix.
[08:56] Sofia Alvarez: Understood. We'll compile and send those. Also, there's an internal redaction tool — for the pilot we recommend you supply the PII rules and we'll run a pre-ingestion filter.
[09:20] Tomas Rivera: How invasive is the pre-ingestion filter? We don't want noticeable latency increase.
[09:25] Markus Li: It's a lightweight parse step. Our tests added ~2-5ms per request on average; for heavy regex sets it can be a bit more, we'll profile it in the bench.
[10:00] Lauren Chen: About the bench — can you remind us the scenarios you'll run? I want them aligned to our real patterns.
[10:06] Sofia Alvarez: Yes: (1) steady-state 50 TPS with 512 token median, (2) spike to 300 TPS with randomized long-tail prompts, (3) long-context sequences 2k tokens, and (4) mixed load with intermittent KV cache invalidations. We'll include regional failover simulation too.
[10:35] Tomas Rivera: can we throw in our sample prompt set?
[10:38] Sofia Alvarez: Please, that's essential. Also include any regex PII rules so we can run the same redaction.
[11:00] Priya Nair: One governance Q: how long do you keep audit logs by default and can we set retention?
[11:06] Markus Li: Default is 90 days, configurable up to 365 in Dedicated/Private; we can push retention to your S3/GCS bucket for longer-term archival.
[12:00] Lauren Chen: Okay, recap me the timeline for pilot prerequisites.
[12:06] Sofia Alvarez: Sure: by Mon 11/16 we need KMS & SSO signoff; by Sun 11/15 you deliver prompt corpus and redaction rules; by Fri 11/13 Redwood shares bench raw logs and trimmed metrics; by Wed 11/18 we provision Dedicated trial and run the 3-hour tail test. Pilot kickoff tentatively 11/20 pending approvals.
[12:50] Tomas Rivera: On the rehydration of cache, what is the expected downtime?
[12:55] Markus Li: It's online migration. We ship serialized entries to the warm pool and step traffic slowly. Expected latency bump minimal, we throttle the migration so it isn't a big tail event.
[13:30] Priya Nair: For the escrow plan, is there a defined handoff if Redwood is unable to meet SLOs for more than N hours? Do we get a credit or an emergency mode?
[13:38] Sofia Alvarez: We propose a two-tier response: immediate automated failover to Dedicated variant; if SLOs are not met for more than 2 hours, an incident bridge escalates and we trigger an emergency credits process and optional on-prem replication for the critical accounts. All subject to the contract terms.
[14:05] Tomas Rivera: That could be good. Also, who's going to manage the canary rollback thresholds?
[14:10] Markus Li: The thresholds are configurable; BluePeak defines the SLA thresholds and we implement automatic rollback based on the agreed tail-latency number. We recommend 99.9th at X ms as the trigger but we'll align with BluePeak's ops.
[15:00] Lauren Chen: Any blockers from Redwood to give us a Dedicated test?
[15:05] Sofia Alvarez: No blockers. We just need a signed trial addendum and some onboarding network details for peering. I'll send those the same day.
[16:00] Tomas Rivera: Do you have any mitigation for sudden KV cache serialization issues? A stopgap we can apply now?
[16:08] Markus Li: We can push a compatibility shim that normalizes the incoming cache serialization format; it's a config flip on the serving runtime. We'll prepare a one-line rollout and a quick revert.
[17:00] Priya Nair: About access controls — can we get role-based access, least privilege, and read-only keys for the SIEM ingest?
[17:06] Sofia Alvarez: Yes RBAC is supported; we'll include an RBAC matrix and sample policies you can import into your IAM.
[18:00] Lauren Chen: This is feeling good. One minor thing — our finance team wants a 30/60/90 cost projection for pilot and for steady state.
[18:08] Sofia Alvarez: We'll extend the cost sheet to include a 90-day projection with the warm standby delta and an estimate for scaling to 3x traffic.
[19:00] Tomas Rivera: Can you include the regression test harness so we can run it internally?
[19:05] Markus Li: We'll give you the harness and a runbook. Some bits are internal but the harness will be runnable with your sample prompts.
[20:00] Lauren Chen: Ok great. Anything else?
[20:05] Priya Nair: Just to emphasize, the CISO office will review the SOC2 and KMS docs before giving final approval.
[20:12] Sofia Alvarez: Understood. We'll prioritize that packet in the email.
[20:40] Tomas Rivera: Quick note — for the bench results please include token-level latency histograms and the raw span traces for the tail. That helped us last time.
[20:50] Markus Li: Noted. We'll include p99.9 and p99.99 histograms and the trace ids so you can correlate.
[22:00] Lauren Chen: Alright, thanks everyone. Let's reconvene after the bench on 11/19 for an initial findings call.
[22:10] Sofia Alvarez: Sounds good. I'll send the trial addendum and the security packet by EOD tomorrow then the bench artifacts Friday.
[22:30] Tomas Rivera: Thank you.
[22:35] Priya Nair: Thanks all.
[22:40] Sofia Alvarez: Bye everyone.

End of call.
